queries: The application of plant essential oils (EOs) in food preservation has gained significant attention due to their dual antibacterial and antioxidant activities, which are primarily attributed to phenolic compounds such as carvacrol, thymol, eugenol, and cinnamaldehyde. These bioactive molecules disrupt microbial cell membranes, inhibit enzymatic activity, and scavenge free radicals, thereby extending the shelf life of perishable products. Key preservation technologies exploiting these properties include active packaging systems, where EOs are incorporated into edible films or coatings (e.g., chitosan, alginate, or starch-based matrices) applied to fresh produce, meat, and seafood; nanoemulsion-based delivery systems that enhance the dispersion and controlled release of EOs in aqueous food matrices; and vapor-phase treatments, where volatile EO compounds are released in headspace to inhibit surface spoilage without direct contact. Additionally, EOs are used in combination with hurdle technologies, such as mild heat, high pressure, or modified atmosphere packaging, to achieve synergistic antimicrobial effects. The scenarios where EOs can replace chemical preservatives include organic and clean-label products, where synthetic additives like sodium benzoate or potassium sorbate are undesirable; minimally processed fresh-cut fruits and vegetables, where EOs in edible coatings reduce microbial load while maintaining sensory quality; and ready-to-eat meat products, where EOs can control pathogens like Listeria monocytogenes. However, the direct replacement is limited by strong sensory impacts, volatility, and concentration-dependent toxicity, necessitating encapsulation or blending with other natural compounds. Thus, EOs serve as viable alternatives in specific applications, particularly when combined with other non-thermal technologies, but their efficacy depends on the food matrix, target microorganisms, and regulatory approval.

candidates.text:
Applications of Essential Oils (EOs) for Food Safety.
For a very long time, EOs have been used in food processing and preservation industries for multiple purposes. Recently, researchers and scientists have focused on antibacterial packaging for food products, edible thin films, effective antibacterial films, nanoemulsions for the preservation of fruits and vegetables, soda/citrus concentrate components, flavoring agents in carbonated colas, soft drinks, and the preservation of meat, fish, and shellfish [73]. EOs are more complex than other types of oils because they contain a variety of naturally occurring bioactive chemicals that are frequently utilized in the food industry as superior substitutes. The antioxidant, antibacterial, and antifungal properties of EOs have been investigated in many research works. EOs obtained from tea tree oil, cinnamon oil, sesame oil, clove oil, lemon oil, chia oil, and thyme oil are only a few examples of oils that have significantly increased antioxidant and antibacterial activity, along with increased cereal storage life and enhanced food security [83]. The key EO groups, such as terpenes and aromatic volatile compounds, contribute to food safety

Several researchers have incorporated various types of EOs such as Thymus capitatus, sunflower, citral and eugenol, cilantro & coriander, clove & clove bud, Ziziphora persica, cinnamon, palmarosa, lemongrass, nettle, thymol, viride, anethum graveolens, mentha, oregano, lemon, nigella sativa, rosemary, neem essential oil, and moringa oil as an active agents in edible coatings and films to shelf life extension of fruits and vege. The addition of essential oils in biopolymer based nanoformulations influenced the flavor and aroma of the fruits and vege in control release, which improving or maintaining the antimicrobial and antioxidant effects for longer period. Many researchers reported that the nanoformulations based on EOs are novel methods to extending the shelf-life of fruits and vege improving their postharvest characteristics. Essential oils (EOs) possess antibacterial, antifungal, and antioxidant properties and are widely used for food preservation. Essential oils (EOs) are natural plants products can be extracted from plant sources and are utilized as preservatives, flavorings, and stabilizers in the food and pharmaceutical industries. The essential oil possesses antimicrobial, antioxidant, antifungal activities due to presence of secondary metabolites and other volatile compounds. Owing to their antimicrobial, antioxidant properties, EOs can also extend the shelf-life of food products. In recent decades, essential oils among the natural products were extensively used as stabilizers, antimicrobial and antioxidant agents to incorporate into food products and packaging materials. In food sectors they can be used in alcoholic & non-alcoholic beverages, gelatins, sweet, soft drinks, milk & dairy products, ice-cream, soft drinks, baked foods, cakes, and candies as flavor and stabilizer agents to enhance the organoleptic and physicochemical properties; on other hands, they can be also used in pharmaceutical sector to improve the taste and flavor of drugs. EOs have also gained attention for their potential use in meat preservation, particularly in poultry. Their natural antimicrobial properties help to inhibit the growth of spoilage microorganisms and pathogens, thus extending the shelf life of meat products. Studies have shown that EOs of oregano, thyme and rosemary effectively reduce the bacterial count in chicken meat, ensuring its safety and quality during storage. The use of these oils represents a natural alternative to synthetic preservatives, meeting consumer demand for more natural methods of food preservation and enhancing food safety by reducing the risk of foodborne illnesses. Despite these promising findings, it is important to point out that high concentrations of EOs are often required to achieve similar effects in situ compared to those established in vitro, leading to negative organoleptic perceptions of products, such as changes in taste and aroma. One possible solution is the combination of different EOs, which can be used in reduced amounts to minimize undesirable aromas and flavours in foods. answer: 根据证据，植物精油（EOs）的抗菌、抗氧化和抗真菌特性被广泛应用于食品保鲜技术中，包括抗菌包装、可食用薄膜、纳米乳液以及水果和蔬菜的保鲜涂层[1][2]。例如，牛至精油（OEO）因含有香芹酚和百里香酚，对曲霉属、镰刀菌属和青霉属等真菌具有广谱抗性，可用于减少真菌污染并延长水果货架期[3]。EOs 还可作为活性剂加入可食用涂层和薄膜中，通过控制释放维持抗菌和抗氧化效果，从而延长食品保质期[2]。在替代化学防腐剂方面，EOs 可用于肉类、鱼类、贝类、谷物、饮料、乳制品、烘焙食品等产品的保鲜和调味，作为天然替代品增强食品安全性[1][4]。此外，纳米乳液等包埋技术能改善EOs的水溶性和稳定性，使其在食品包装中更有效地释放活性成分，减少对合成防腐剂的依赖[3]。总体而言，EOs 在食品加工、包装和储存中提供了环保且高效的化学防腐剂替代方案[1][3]。
